# Phase 3 — driver ranking

*Generated by `hydrocascade rootcause` on 2026-09-17.*

> ### ⚠ Fitted on synthetic data
>
> `data_mode` is `synthetic` for `era5_land`, `glofas`, `imd`, `imerg`, and 9,764 of
> 9,765 catalog rows are synthetic stand-ins. **Every number in this report describes
> the stand-in generators, not Kerala.** They are here to show the procedure runs end
> to end and that the diagnostics fire. Switching `data_mode` to `real` and rerunning
> `hydrocascade rootcause` turns all of them into results with no code change.


Doc 06 §4: three methods, reported together, because each is wrong in a different way and agreement between them is the evidence. Permutation importance is computed on the **held-out spatial blocks** — on training rows it measures memorisation, not importance.

## Landslide

| 1 | `R7` | +0.303 | +0.2937 | 0.9028 | A week of rain raises the water table rather than the wetting front. |
| 2 | `slope_max_deg` | +0.305 | +0.1305 | 0.8913 | The steepest facet within a unit is where failure initiates, so the maximum matters more than the mean for triggering, and the mean more for runout. |
| 3 | `twi` | -0.233 | +0.1825 | 0.7088 | ln(a/tan B) is a steady-state index of how much upslope water converges here per unit gradient. High TWI means saturation, which raises pore pressure and cancels frictional strength. |

| 6 | `relief_m` | +0.272 | +0.0334 | 0.2332 | Local relief is the potential energy available to a failure — it sets how far debris can travel once moving. |
| 7 | `elev_mean_m` | +0.007 | +0.0880 | 0.3380 | Elevation proxies orographic rainfall and regolith age; it is a correlate of the cause rather than a cause. |
| 8 | `eastness` | -0.058 | +0.0471 | 0.1402 | East-west aspect separates windward from leeward of the south-west monsoon. |

| 10 | `curv_prof` | +0.058 | +0.0369 | 0.1397 | Concave profile curvature decelerates flow and lets water and colluvium accumulate; it marks the hollows where shallow landslides repeatedly initiate. |
| 11 | `d_slope_km` | +0.042 | +0.0309 | 0.1439 | Flow-path distance to the channel. Short d_slope means debris reaches a stream and becomes a flood problem; long d_slope means it stops on the hillside. |

### Stability across negative-sampling ratios — Doc 06 §2

✅ The top 3 drivers were the same set across all 3 sampling ratios, with the order changing (1:1 → R7, slope_max_deg, twi; 1:5 → R7, slope_max_deg, twi; 1:20 → slope_max_deg, R7, twi).

| ratio | 1st | 2nd | 3rd | 4th |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1:1 | `R7` | `slope_max_deg` | `twi` | `drainage_density_km_km2` |
| 1:5 | `R7` | `slope_max_deg` | `twi` | `R3` |
| 1:20 | `slope_max_deg` | `R7` | `twi` | `R3` |

### `e~(u)` — what Phase 4 receives

Doc 06 §4 caps this at two to four standardised drivers: *every additional driver here costs identifiability in the cascade model that we cannot afford.* Exported to `data/processed/top_drivers.json`.

Selected: `R7`, `slope_max_deg`, `twi`, `R3`
